title: Newborn Jaundice: Common and Usually Harmless
hook: Many newborns turn a little yellow in the first days — jaundice is common, usually harmless, and often clears on its own, but a few warning signs mean get it checked promptly.
key_points: Jaundice is yellowing of the skin and eyes, most noticeable around day 3; it's very common and usually harmless.
It often resolves on its own by about two weeks without treatment.
Get urgent advice if jaundice appears in the first 24 hours, the baby is very sleepy, feeds poorly, or it lasts beyond two weeks.
When treatment is needed, phototherapy (a special light) helps the baby's body clear the bilirubin.
content_html: Don't be alarmed if your newborn looks a little yellow in the first days — jaundice is one of the most common newborn conditions. It shows as a yellow tinge to the skin and the whites of the eyes (which can be harder to spot on darker skin), and for most babies it's most noticeable around day 3. In the great majority of cases it's harmless and clears on its own by about two weeks.
extra_html: That said, the NHS flags a few situations that need prompt attention: jaundice that appears in the first 24 hours of life, a baby who is very sleepy or feeding poorly, or jaundice that lasts beyond two weeks. When treatment is needed, phototherapy — placing the baby under a special light — helps their body clear the bilirubin and is generally very effective with few side effects. This is general guidance; if you're ever unsure about your baby's colour, feeding, or alertness, contact your midwife or doctor right away.

related.title: Well-Child Visits: Your Regular Check-Ups
related.hook: Well-child visits aren't just for when something's wrong — they track growth and development, deliver vaccines on schedule, and catch problems early, even when your child seems perfectly fine.

related.title: When to Call the Doctor — Red Flags
related.hook: Most childhood illnesses are mild, but a handful of signs mean don't wait and watch — get medical help right away. Knowing them takes the guesswork out of a scary moment.

related.title: The Routine Tests and Shot of the First Days
related.hook: In the first days, a healthy newborn gets a heel-prick blood screen, a hearing check, a heart-oxygen check, and a vitamin K shot — quick, routine steps that catch rare but serious problems early.

flashcards.prompt: When is newborn jaundice usually most noticeable?

choices.text: Immediately at the moment of birth

flashcards.explanation_html: For most babies the yellow tinge is most noticeable around day 3. It's common and usually clears on its own by about two weeks.

flashcards.prompt: Which jaundice sign means you should seek advice urgently?

choices.text: Yellowing in the first 24 hours, a very sleepy baby, or poor feeding
Mild yellowing at day 3 that's improving

flashcards.explanation_html: Jaundice within the first 24 hours, a very sleepy baby, poor feeding, or jaundice lasting beyond two weeks all warrant prompt medical advice.

flashcards.prompt: What treatment is used when newborn jaundice needs it?
flashcards.back_html: Phototherapy — shining a special light on the baby's skin, which helps their body break down and clear the bilirubin.
